text: Book-Smart, Not Street-Smart states that smart contracts privilege technical form while excluding the social contexts and complex human uses within which contracts operate. This independently corresponds to Kaal's criticism that code-is-law substitutes technical protocols for interpretive flexibility and normative deliberation. The proposition does not assess Kaal's proposed legal remedy.
